## The question

How do governments decide what time people live by? Debates about daylight saving time bring scientific arguments into contact with economic interests, public preferences and institutional constraints.

## The project

Examine the politics of seasonal clock changes through a focused policy study. Trace how evidence and competing values enter decision-making in a defined jurisdiction or comparison, distinguishing policy proposals from decisions that have actually taken effect.

## What you will do

- Identify relevant policy documents, public consultations and institutional actors.
- Develop a transparent document analysis or comparative case-study approach.
- Analyse how arguments, interests and responsibilities shape the policy process.

## Possible scope

A thesis could investigate one policy process in depth or compare carefully selected cases. A shorter placement could map documents and actors. Political science, public policy or documentary research experience would fit well.
